title: Adaptive Plan Gatekeeper with Grace-Period Credit Smoothing
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Goal: Implement a gatekeeper admission controller that enforces tiered access (free / paid / enterprise) while smoothing short-term quota churn via a configurable grace period and credit-smoothing algorithm. This feature should prioritize higher-tier requests when capacity or token budgets are scarce, allow short bursts for healthy UX on free/paid tiers, and avoid oscillation-induced unfairness across tenants.

Scope:
- Admission policy service that evaluates requests by tenant plan, remaining quota, recent consumption rate, and per-tenant latency SLOs.
- Grace-period credits: allow temporary overage/burst for a configured window (e.g., 30s–5m) and amortize its cost against slower quota depletion afterward.
- Soft fallback paths: when the primary model or tier capacity is constrained, route to cheaper model variants (quantized or smaller) for free/paid tiers and to reserved variants for enterprise.
- Integrate with existing token accounting and billing signals; emit detailed telemetry for per-plan cost/latency impact.
- Rollout: feature flagged, default-off for host, opt-in for Dedicated, opt-in per-customer for Private.

Acceptance Criteria:
1) Policy engine enforces priority ordering (enterprise > paid > free) with configurable weight multipliers.
2) Grace-period smoothing reduces short-term request drops by at least 45% on synthetic burst tests while keeping longer-term budget enforcement intact.
3) Fallback routing chooses compatible model variant within latency budget and logs decision trace for each routed request.
4) No regression in 95th percentile latency for enterprise traffic (+/- 5%).
5) Unit and integration tests cover admission decisions, credit amortization, and fallback selection.

Non-goals:
- Full billing adjustments or invoicing changes (billing team to handle final charge reconciliation).
- Per-customer SLA negotiation UI (console UX ticket to follow).

Constraints & Trade-offs:
- Aggressive smoothing increases short-term cost; we will cap aggregate burst budget per plan class to control spend.
- Consistency vs latency: to keep admission logic fast we use eventual counters with sketching (count-min/decayed counters) rather than global strong-consistency quota locks.

Design sketch:
1) Admission path receives (tenant_id, plan, request_size, model_hint, region) and queries local cache for: remaining_quota_estimate, recent_rate (EWMA), burst_credits_left.
2) Compute score = base_priority_weight(plan) - alpha * rate_normalized + beta * burst_credit_factor. If score above threshold -> accept on primary lane. Else try fallback variants in prioritized list.
3) If fallback chosen, annotate trace with fallback_reason and model_variant_id. If no variant fits latency/cost constraints, reply with soft-reject providing retry-after and suggested variant.
4) On accept, decrement amortized quota (apply fractional deduction if using grace credits). Persist write-back asynchronously to global accounting to avoid tail latency.

Monitoring & Metrics:
- Per-plan accepted_rate, rejected_rate, fallback_rate, avg_latency, cost_per_token_estimate.
- Burst credit usage and amortization backlog.
- Customer-impact alerts if enterprise rejection > 0.1%.

Rollout plan:
- Canary in staging for 48h with synthetic bursts.
- Canary in hosted for low-traffic region (us-west-2) for 72h.
- Ramp to 20% traffic with feature flag, monitor for cost/latency regressions.
- Full rollout gated on SLO and cost thresholds.

Notes on compatibility:
- Backward compatible with existing routing table; if feature disabled, admission falls back to current soft-reserve router.
- Fallback variant catalog managed by model-onboarding; unit tests will include model compatibility matrix samples.
